s0.why: Sentence 1 calls him an American geologist, a WWII Navy officer and one of the founding fathers of plate tectonics.

s1.why: 20 makes him captain of an attack transport, 22 has him continuously using the echo sounder, 23 gives the North Pacific profiles and the guyots he named.

s2.why: 25-26 date the report to 1960 and state crust moving laterally from volcanically active ridges; 28 says the process was later named seafloor spreading.

f0.why: Sentence 1 gives exactly May 24, 1906 to August 25, 1969.

f1.why: 20 names the USS Cape Johnson, an attack transport ship equipped with sonar.

f2.why: 23 says he discovered flat-topped submarine volcanoes and termed them guyots.

f3.why: 30 gives the title and 1962 and calls it a much-referenced work, but never says it is a book; the label adds that (it was a paper).

f4.why: 24 says he stayed in the Naval Reserve, rising to the rank of rear admiral.

q1.why: 22 says he continuously used his ship's echo sounder and 23 says this surveying gave him the North Pacific profiles.

q2.why: 28 says seafloor spreading made Wegener's earlier, generally dismissed continental drift scientifically respectable.

q3.why: 23 identifies the flat-topped features as submarine volcanoes.

q4.why: 26 says the report argued crust moved laterally away from long, volcanically active oceanic ridges.

q5.why: 2 says he suggested convection in the Earth's mantle is the driving force of the process.

q6.why: 27 says he only understood the profiles after Tharp and Heezen discovered the Great Global Rift along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
